text:
Morgan Geekie had no goals in six games, then scored in four straight, including a power-play one-timer. The Hockey Writers and Heavy both noticed the turnaround from a slow start. He has 5 goals and 14 points in 18 games.

His finishing is right where it should be, 5 goals on 5.8 expected. Last season he scored 39, and Evolving-Hockey said he was even better than that by chance quality (3.5 expected wins against 1.6 actual). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why he scores: he's on the receiving end of royal-road passes more than most.

The assists are the softer part. Boston has scored 7.6 more goals than expected with him on, so his nine assists come with help, and the Bruins get only 51% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, a couple of points worse than without him. His ice time is down almost two minutes recently too. Watch the minutes: the goal streak earned him attention, but the coach is trimming his role, not growing it.
headline: Geekie found his shot again
